sub_questions.question: What settings control how much context the retrieval node returns (sometimes too much, sometimes almost nothing)?

claims.claim: top_k on the retrieval node sets the maximum number of chunks returned.
The score threshold is optional and discards any chunk scoring below the cutoff, even if it would otherwise be within top_k.
claims.guide_evidence: an optional score threshold (chunks scoring below it are discarded even if they would otherwise be in the top_k)

claims.claim: To reduce excess context, lower top_k or raise the score threshold.
claims.guide_evidence: top_k (how many chunks to return), an optional score threshold (chunks scoring below it are discarded

claims.claim: Getting almost nothing back may be caused by a score threshold set too high or by the query not matching much in the dataset.
claims.guide_evidence: A retrieval step that returns no results is most often explained by the score threshold being set too high, the document still being mid-indexing, or the query simply not matching any ingested content

claims.claim: Hit Testing on the dataset lets you try queries and see the actual retrieval scores.
claims.guide_evidence: the Hit Testing / retrieval-test panel on the dataset page lets a builder type a sample query and see exactly which chunks would be retrieved and their similarity scores

evaluation.rationale: Every claim in the answer matches the guide's description of the retrieval node: top_k, the optional score threshold, the causes of empty results, and Hit Testing. It could also have mentioned reranking, documents still being indexed, and Parent-Child chunking, which returns larger parent chunks. Leaving these out doesn't make anything it says wrong, so it is safe to send.
